lines: One-week history of double vision worsening with left gaze
This 36-year-old female with established multiple sclerosis returns for evaluation of new visual symptoms, following prior neurology visits in 2020 for intermittent numbness and blurred vision.
She reports that the double vision worsens when looking to the left and improves when closing either eye.
She also mentions occasional episodes of tingling in her hands and feet over the past few months.
Her past medical history is significant for an episode of optic neuritis two years ago, which resolved without intervention.
- Open reduction and internal fixation of pelvis following traumatic fracture (2 years prior)
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (1-2 inhalations) every 4-6 hours as needed for asthma symptoms
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Social (2-3 drinks per week). Occupation: Marketing Manager.
On examination, when asked to look to the left, her right eye fails to adduct and the left eye exhibits nystagmus.
Her visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and the rest of the cranial nerve examination is normal.
Sensation is intact, but she has hyperreflexia in both lower extremities.
MRI of the brain with gadolinium contrast shows multiple periventricular white matter lesions.
